claims.says: Jun-Aug
Late April through June generally offers the most consolidated snow/ice and the least glacier crevassing; by July the glacier is more broken up...
May through early July, when ice and seracs are frozen and most stable
May: optimal, June: good, July: marginal, April: risky
Spring, roughly Apr-May, when the route is in as snow and ice

contradictions.why: The stated season (Jun-Aug) starts after the route's own best_season/seasonal_guidance say conditions are already declining (July rated only 'marginal', August not mentioned as good at all), while April-June — mostly outside the stated season — is repeatedly called the best window.
contradictions.internal_resolution: best_season, seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow, monthBreakdown, and an approach_variant all independently agree the route is best climbed April/May-June/early July; the top-level 'season' field (Jun-Aug) is the outlier.

claims.says: Descend via the Sherpa Glacier (starting near the false summit, ~8,200 ft) back into the basin below the Sherpa/Ice Cliff glaciers, then retrace the approach to the Stuart Lake Trailhead. Do not down-climb the ice route.
Descend via the Sherpa Glacier, starting near the false summit (~8,200 ft), back down into the basin below the Sherpa and Ice Cliff glaciers, then retrace the approach to the Stuart Lake Trailhead.
Descend the Cascadian, not the route
Descend Cascadian Couloir to Ingalls Creek / Exit over Longs Pass
Climb the Ice Cliff Glacier to the summit, descend Cascadian
Descend by the Sherpa Glacier or the Cascadian Couloir; do not reverse the ice route.

contradictions.why: descent and descent_text both definitively describe returning via the Sherpa Glacier to the SAME (Stuart Lake, north-side) trailhead, while pro_tips, the itinerary schedule, and timing.sectionBreakdown all describe exiting via the Cascadian Couloir to Ingalls Creek and over Longs Pass to a completely different (south-side) trailhead — a climber would plan car logistics very differently depending on which field they read.
contradictions.internal_resolution: descent and descent_text agree with each other and are the most explicit, purpose-built DESCENT fields; no waypoint in this route names Longs Pass, Ingalls Creek, or the Cascadian Couloir (unlike the North Ridge route, whose own itinerary uses near-identical wording 'Descend Cascadian Couloir to Ingalls Creek' / 'Exit over Longs Pass'), suggesting the itinerary/timing/pro_tips Cascadian references are contamination copied from a different Stuart route.

contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoints list and the approach_variants text (a separate field) agree with each other on 'Ingalls Pass'; the top-level 'approach' field's 'Longs Pass' mention is the outlier and appears to misname the pass.

contradictions.fact: Bergschrund/glacier hazard on a rock-route approach that has no glacier

claims.says: Bergschrund crossing at base of climbers' trail—may require downclimbing on snow/ice; assess conditions carefully in spring/early summer
hike... to Longs Pass... continue past Ingalls Lake toward Stuart Pass, then follow the climbers' trail onto the talus shoulder... contour northwest to Goat Pass

contradictions.why: The route's approach is entirely trail/talus (no glacier is mentioned anywhere in approach, hazards, or obj_haz), yet watch_out asserts a bergschrund crossing — a glacier feature — which nothing else in the route corroborates.
contradictions.internal_resolution: No other field (approach, hazards, obj_haz, approach_variants) mentions a glacier or bergschrund on this route; likely contamination from a glaciated Stuart route (e.g. Ice Cliff Glacier or North Ridge).

contradictions.fact: Standard descent route and exit trailhead

claims.says: Descend the north side, back to the basin you camped in... returns you to the Ice Cliff/Sherpa moraine camp, then out the Mountaineer Creek climbers' trail to the Stuart Lake trailhead. ...Continuing over the summit and down the Cascadian Couloir to Longs Pass is possible but exits at a trailhead roughly 70 road miles away and abandons your camp; sources treat it as a penalty rather than the plan.

...descend as for the standard south-side line: east ridge toward the false summit... then down the broad Cascadian Couloir... to Ingalls Creek, and back out over Longs Pass to the Esmeralda Basin/Ingalls Creek trailhead... a car shuttle (or a long overland return) is part of planning this route as a car-to-car day.
Descend the Cascadian Couloir and exit over Longs Pass
outback

contradictions.why: descent explicitly says the standard, planned descent returns north to the SAME camp/trailhead and calls the Cascadian-to-Longs-Pass option an unplanned 'penalty' 70 road miles away; descent_text and the itinerary schedule instead present the Cascadian/Longs Pass/Esmeralda exit AS the standard descent, requiring a car shuttle to a different trailhead entirely.
contradictions.internal_resolution: loss_ft (6000) and the itinerary's own day totals (loss ≈6200) closely match a return to the same Stuart Lake trailhead (9415-3400≈6015), not the Esmeralda exit (9415-4269≈5146); outing_shape='outback' (out-and-back) also matches the descent field's same-camp return rather than descent_text's cross-mountain loop with a shuttle. descent + gain/loss + outing_shape agree with each other; descent_text and the itinerary schedule's Cascadian narrative are the contradicting outlier, likely contamination from a route that genuinely does exit via Longs Pass (e.g. North Ridge or Stuart Glacier Couloir).

contradictions.why: The same route names the same trailhead at two elevations 610 ft apart, well over the ~250 ft materiality threshold.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft (6000) is much closer to 9415-3540≈5875 than to 9415-2930≈6485, and this trailhead is listed at ~3,400-3,540 ft on every other Mount Stuart route in this dataset, so the waypoint's 2,930 ft figure looks like the outlier.
